### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class), saveMetaItem (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via saveMetaItem (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via saveMetaItem (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via saveMetaItem (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via saveMetaItem (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **14** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 570f01d270a37aeadfe078a6892797428151a7a8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `94b77b47982ca81cb2969f3d230538f571c55e66` — the merge of head `4a199348b9729b7f3e2a52d5340789a1d284cba7` into base `570f01d270a37aeadfe078a6892797428151a7a8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 94b77b47982ca81cb2969f3d230538f571c55e66 && git checkout 94b77b47982ca81cb2969f3d230538f571c55e66
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 570f01d270a37aeadfe078a6892797428151a7a8 4a199348b9729b7f3e2a52d5340789a1d284cba7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 570f01d270a37aeadfe078a6892797428151a7a8 && git merge --no-ff 4a199348b9729b7f3e2a52d5340789a1d284cba7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 570f01d270a37aeadfe078a6892797428151a7a8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 570f01d270a37aeadfe078a6892797428151a7a8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4a199348b9729b7f3e2a52d5340789a1d284cba7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.save-flow-canonicalization.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/canonicalize-stored-flow.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-flow-save-retired-spelling.test.ts, .changeset/23775-flow-save-door-new-refusal.md + packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts (`headAt`, `resolveWriteHead`), packages/spec/src/conversions/apply.ts (`applyConversionsToFlow`, `includeRetired`), packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts (the 13 `retiredFromLoadPath` flow entries, `flow-node-http-callout-rename`), packages/spec/src/conversions/conversions.test.ts (the kept-without-ruling list), packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts (`IAutomationService.canonicalizeStoredFlow?`), packages/metadata-core/src/item-key-discriminators.ts (`itemDiscriminator`), packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts (`registerAndSaveFlow`, the clone door), packages/runtime/src/flow-clone.ts (`cloneFlowDefinition`), packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.ts (the ceremony's `door.save` types), packages/mcp/src (no metadata-write tool), packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts, objectui at the pinned `.objectui-sha` `daeb77fc84` — packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx (`saveFlowDraft`, `doCreateFlow`, `withStartTrigger`, `publishDraft`) and skeletons.ts (`buildFlowSkeleton`)

Read against ruling 6212082860 (letter B, six items), the card body and all five comments, PR #23902's body and seven-file list, the net three-dot diff against `main` at `570f01d27` (+692 / −57, identical to GitHub's file list), the head's check-runs, and the `os-dev-report` 6215320435.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Ruling item 2, the new-flow arm — right.** `saveMetaItem`'s flow branch (protocol.ts head `:23031`) asks `flowSaveReplaysRetired` once, before the canonicalizer is resolved, and hands the answer to BOTH hosts: the engine call `canonicalizeFlow(request.name, request.item, { includeRetired })` and the no-engine fallback `applyConversionsToFlow(request.item, { includeRetired, excludeConversionIds: FLOW_FALLBACK_VERDICT_NOT_REPLAYED })` (`:23100`). With the window closed, `apply.ts:156` skips every `retiredFromLoadPath` entry, the spelling stays in place, and the schema gate (`:23130`) refuses it `422 INVALID_METADATA` with located `issues`. On an engine host the strict parse throws first; the throw is caught, `result` is dropped, and the same fallback verdict reaches the same 422 — the #21982 parity holds on both hosts. The text-equality pin against `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse(normalizeStackInput(...))` proves the prescription is the authoring funnel's own. Accept-set change: the API save door's accept set for a NEW flow narrows by exactly the 12 retired flow spellings the loader stopped lifting (see ② item 5) — the change ruling item 4 declares.
2. **Ruling item 2, the re-save arm — right.** A stored row at the save's address answers `true`, so the full chain (`includeRetired: true`) is replayed exactly as before; the engine stub and the real-stack REST pins both re-save a seeded legacy row and read it back served. The engine's rehydration is untouched: `registerFlow` (engine.ts head `:4642`) still calls `canonicalizeFlow(name, definition)` with no options, and `options.includeRetired ?? true` keeps the chain open for every caller that passes nothing (`:4595`). The read path is untouched: no hunk reaches `getMetaItem`/`getMetaItems`, and the "read path serves stored flows verbatim" sentence stands at `:22989`.
3. **Ruling item 1, the predicate — right in substance, with ONE named deviation from the parenthetical, and the deviation is the ruling's own premise falsified by a measurement, not a re-ruling.** The ruling says the predicate is read "with the lookup the door already makes for its baseline (the OCC / version read)". Measured on the head: the OCC read (`writeHead = await repo.headAt(...)`, `:23517`) sits after `ensureOverlayIndex()` (`:23381`) and after the schema gate, so it runs AFTER the canonicalization it would have to decide, and for a draft save it reads the draft head alone. The implementation therefore reads the OTHER baseline the door already makes — `authoredLockFamily` (`:22221-22225`) and `storedBodyForCarryForward` (`:9443-9455`): `headAt` at the save's own state and package, then for a draft save with no draft row the ACTIVE row at the inherited binding `target.packageId`. The predicate's two reads are byte-for-byte the shape of those two readers (same `ref` with `org: 'env'`, same `itemDiscriminator` member, same `packageId ?? null` then `target.packageId`), it runs at the same position in the method as `authoredLockFamily` (before `ensureOverlayIndex`, with that precedent), and `headAt` is the write-address resolution `put` itself locks against (sys-metadata-repository.ts `resolveWriteHead`), so "the row the save overwrites" is read with the repository's own answer, draft inheritance (#11087, #23297, #23657) included. The main clause of item 1 holds; the parenthetical could not. The draft-to-active fallback is what item 2's "a legacy row stays editable in Studio" requires: verified at the pinned objectui `daeb77fc84`, `StudioDesignSurface.tsx:6944` and `:7009` save flows with `{ mode: 'draft', packageId: draftPackageId }`, so Studio's first edit of a stored active flow has no draft row and would be judged new without it (ablation leg 3 is the dev's measurement of exactly that). The mode does not change the predicate's meaning — new refuses in both modes (pinned in draft and publish, both hosts, protocol and REST).
4. **Ruling item 2's "a legacy row stays editable in Studio" — right, and Studio's CREATE is safe too.** `doCreateFlow` (pinned objectui `:6864`) writes `buildFlowSkeleton` (start → end, canonical keys only) plus `withStartTrigger` (`config.triggerType` / `config.objectName` on the start node — declared keys, no retired spelling) with `status: 'obsolete'`, so a new Studio flow meets no refusal. Studio's publish is a promotion (`shellClient.publishDraft('flow', …)` → `publishMetaItem` → `promoteDraftForPublish`, which never calls `saveMetaItem`), so no Studio path reaches the flow branch in publish mode.
5. **The server-stated writes exemption (`source` set, `writeFace: 'package-duplicate' | 'package-unmanaged-import'` answer `true` with no read) — right; not named by any ruling item, consistent with the governing text.** The ruling's letter speaks only of a flow "with no stored row at the save's address" and of "a re-save of an existing row"; a package duplicate writes a copy of a stored row to a NEW address and an unmanaged import writes a built artifact's flows to names no row held, so the literal predicate would judge both as authored. Read in the code: `duplicatePackage` (`:27639`) and `importUnmanagedPackage` (`:27873`, `prepared[].item = result.storable`) both pre-canonicalize through the engine's full chain where an engine is reachable, and `migrateStoredMetadata` (`:24265`) and `flow-credential-migration.ts:222` state `source: 'migrate-stored'` for rewrites of rows at rest. The ADR-0087 2026-07-31 addendum names `duplicatePackage` among the seams that "replay the FULL chain, retired entries included" and rules that "a row at rest has no author to teach"; judging these as authored would refuse, on a no-engine host only, what an engine host accepts — the verdict split #21982 closed — and would refuse data at rest, which is option C, not taken. Only these three faces are exempt; `'meta-envelope'` (REST), `'meta-dispatch'` (runtime dispatcher) and `'external-import'` (object only) stay authoring faces. The exemption is a reading the maintainer can confirm (③ item 2); it is not a deviation from a ruling item.
6. **Every other in-repo flow writer reaches the right verdict — right.** `registerAndSaveFlow` (runtime automation.ts `:1802`, the `POST /automation` definition and `POST /:name/clone` doors) registers in the engine first (full chain) and then calls `saveMetaItem({ type: 'flow', name, item: definition })` with no face: a NEW definition carrying a retired spelling is refused by the door and the registration is withdrawn (`restoreFlowRegistration`), so the changeset's "every caller of the protocol" holds; a clone copies the engine's live `FlowParsed` (`cloneFlowDefinition` deep-copies `getFlow(name)`, which `registerFlow` stored post-chain), so a legacy source clones in the canonical spelling and meets no refusal. The organization-ownership ceremony's `door.save` writes `position`, `permission`, `view` and `email_template` only — no flow. `packages.ts:1787` writes `app`. No in-repo writer is regressed.
7. **`AutomationEngine.canonicalizeStoredFlow(name, definition, options?)` — right; ruling item 4's "service-automation canonicalizer option".** An additive optional third parameter on a public class method, default `true`, threaded into the private `canonicalizeFlow`; the default-flip exclusion (`CONVERSIONS_NOT_REPLAYED_AT_REHYDRATION`) applies whatever the option says. Public-surface change: a widening of `@objectstack/service-automation`'s runtime surface. The spec contract `IAutomationService.canonicalizeStoredFlow?(name, definition)` (`automation-service.ts:853`) is NOT changed — compatible (an implementation may take an extra optional parameter; Type Check green), and the protocol reads the method structurally and passes `options` only when it holds one (`resolveFlowCanonicalizer`, `:6576`). The gap this leaves is a boundary flag (③ item 4), not a defect of this PR's lane.
8. **The #4580 warning relocation — right, implied by B.** `flowCanonicalizeFallback` is captured in the `catch` and said only after the schema gate has accepted the body (`:23216`), deduped by the same key. On a new flow the canonicalizer's throw is now usually the retired spelling's refusal, which the gate answers 422; "was saved WITHOUT canonicalization" there would have claimed a save that never happened. Outside the claim's strict flow-branch lines, inside protocol.ts and flow-only; the pre-existing case of a later gate refusing after the warning is narrowed, not widened (dev's acceptance note, accurate).
9. **Ruling item 3, the pins — right for protocol and REST; MCP NOT MEASURED, and not constructible here.** Protocol (`protocol.save-flow-canonicalization.test.ts`, 34 tests): new flow with a retired spelling → 422 at `nodes.0.config.filters` naming `filter`, nothing stored, no #4580 warning, on an engine stub that honours `includeRetired` and on a no-engine host, in draft and publish mode; canonical new flow saves; stored legacy row re-saves and is served; stored legacy DRAFT re-saves; the option spy sees `{ includeRetired: false }` on the new flow and `{ includeRetired: true }` on the re-save; issue-text equality with the authoring funnel; the two server-stated faces keep the full chain. Existing #4542 / #21982 pins now seed the row they re-save (`seedStoredFlow`), their subject unchanged. REST (`meta-flow-save-retired-spelling.test.ts`, real stack, better-sqlite3 memory, 6 tests): the loose key beside its block → 422 at `nodes.1.config.duration` naming `waitEventConfig.timerDuration`; the bare loose key → 422 at `nodes.1.waitEventConfig` naming `timerDuration` (the node rule answers first — the same two-round behaviour `os validate` has, as the dev notes); draft mode refuses too; canonical saves; stored legacy row re-saves and `GET` serves it; Studio's first draft over a stored active row saves. Engine (`canonicalize-stored-flow.test.ts`, 6 tests): no option lifts; `false` refuses at the written key or at the block; `false` is a no-op (reference-identical) on a canonical body; `true` equals the default; `registerFlow` still registers the legacy spelling. MCP: `packages/mcp/src` registers no `saveMetaItem` caller and no `create_metadata` / `update_metadata` tool — those names live in `platform-tool-names.ts:60,83` for the cloud repository's `service-ai-studio`; a pin there is outside this repository (③ item 3).
10. **Ruling item 5, the order — right.** F2 landed on `main` (`f606ba2e2`, PR #23810) before the branch's merge of `origin/main` `34b740f2d`; `retry-policy-converged` is `retiredFromLoadPath: true` at head (`registry.ts:4287`) and therefore in the changeset's marker and migration list. `flow-node-http-callout-rename` (F5-http) is still live-window (`conversions.test.ts:404`, the kept list) and correctly absent — under B it meets the same refusal on the day its own PR retires it, with no change here. PR #23854's `engine.ts` hunks merged cleanly and the diff touches only the `canonicalizeStoredFlow` / `canonicalizeFlow` region; no view-node function of PR #23836 is touched.
11. **Ruling item 6, the ADR line — right.** One dated blockquote note plus one blank line, inside `## Addendum (2026-07-31)` (head `:534-575`, note at `:574`), naming the predicate, the draft-overlays-active clause, the 422 text and the server-stated exemption; no existing line changed (+2 / −0). The addendum is not rewritten.
12. **The 13th retired flow entry is rightly absent.** `flow-decision-mode-inclusive-explicit` (`registry.ts`, toMajor 18, retired) is a DEFAULT FLIP excluded by name at both seams regardless of `includeRetired` (`FLOW_FALLBACK_VERDICT_NOT_REPLAYED`, protocol.ts; `CONVERSIONS_NOT_REPLAYED_AT_REHYDRATION`, engine.ts; ruling letter C on #15429), so the door never replayed it and this PR changes nothing about it — its absence from the changeset's marker and migration list is correct, and the dev's "12 retired flow D2 ids" count is the right one.
13. **The confidence-gap premise — holds.** No in-repo producer writes a retired flow spelling (card premise 3, re-run by the director and the dev; the only non-test hits are the registry's own entries and `migrations/registry.ts.template`); the designer writes blocks (item 4 above). The visible change is confined to an external client that CREATES a flow in a retired spelling, which is the ruling's intended effect.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/23775-flow-save-door-new-refusal.md`: `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': minor`, `'@objectstack/service-automation': minor`; header `feat(metadata-protocol)!:`; body carries `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` — the same line the PR body carries — a `**BREAKING (API save door)**` paragraph, the FROM → TO migration for every refused spelling, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `adr-0087: not-required (already-registered …)` naming the 12 retired flow D2 ids.
- **Level — right.** `metadata-protocol` publishes a narrowed runtime accept set (BREAKING under AGENTS.md §Post-Task 3: "`(narrowing)` is BREAKING"); `major` is barred in the launch window (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, question 1), and every narrowing landed on `main` in this line took `minor` with `feat(…)!:` + BREAKING + migration (F2 `f606ba2e2`, F3 `d176b0aab`, F4 `105902f10`, #23447 `a35f7a676`) — this changeset matches that shape exactly. `service-automation` publishes an additive optional parameter on a public method: `minor` is the right level for a widening. Both packages are published (`18.0.0-next.2`, not private). `@objectstack/rest` gains a test file only and `@objectstack/spec` is untouched — neither owes a changeset. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- **Migration — complete and accurate.** Each of the 12 ids' FROM → TO lines matches the registry entry's own `summary` (`filters → filter`; `object → objectName`; notify `to/subject/body/url → recipients/title/message/actionUrl`, `source: {object,id} → sourceObject/sourceId`; wait loose `duration/timerDuration/signal/signalName/eventType → waitEventConfig.*`, block `timeoutMs → timerDuration`, `onTimeout` removed; connector `connectorId/actionId/input → connectorConfig`; `flow → flowName` on map and subflow; script `functionName → function`, `input → inputs`, `actionType/template/recipients/variables/script` removed; `active/template/outputSchema/errorHandling.fallbackNodeId` removed; `retryDelayMs → backoffMs`). Stored rows need nothing — stated. `os migrate meta --from 16` named as the source-file counterpart — right.
- **ADR-0087 marker — right category.** `already-registered`: every named id resolves at head and pre-exists this diff (none is added here; `retry-policy-converged` was retired by F2 on `main`), and the change retires nothing from the registry — it only stops the door replaying those entries for authored input. `check:adr-0087-registration` ran green in the head's Lint jobs.
- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` — right**, on the PR body and the changeset alike; it is the arm ruling item 4 prescribes, and the record you are reading is the review that arm owes at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Dev deviation 1 / `open_questions[0]` (predicate scope for a draft save: OCC read only, or the door's baseline with the active-row fallback) — answered: B, as implemented; the confirmation is escalated to the maintainer, where it already sits.** The dispatch's needs-decision clause was conditioned on a mechanism assumption the dev measured false (① item 3); ruling items 1 (main clause) and 2 together decide the reading, and A would refuse Studio's first edit of every legacy flow on the main human door against item 2's own words. A ruling's interpretation is the maintainer's: the PR body's 维护者速读 names this reading as the first thing to confirm, and the Tier H approval on `docs/adr/**` is that confirmation. No re-ruling is needed; reverting to A is deleting the three-line active fallback.
2. **Dev deviation 2 / `open_questions[1]` (server-stated writes keep the full chain) — answered: B, as implemented; escalated to the maintainer the same way.** ① item 5 gives the reading in the code and the governing text; the literal predicate would split the verdict by host and refuse data at rest. The PR body names it as the second thing to confirm at approval.
3. **Dev deviation 4 / `open_questions[2]` (ruling item 3's MCP door) — answered: option A, a cloud-lane card; escalated to the dispatching PM seat (`session_01TQLy3Yq6vF4SDpTXdr3Uwi`, the claim 6212892799 holder) to file against the cloud repository's `service-ai-studio` (`create_metadata` / `update_metadata`).** Verified: nothing in `packages/mcp/src` writes metadata, so no pin is constructible in objectstack; this PR cannot carry it, and the ruling's MCP clause stays NOT MEASURED until that card lands. Not a FAIL ground here — the ruling placed the lane in `domain:engine` with the in-repo doors, and every in-repo door reaches the one `saveMetaItem` this PR pins.
4. **Dev acceptance note 1 (the spec contract does not name the option) — escalated to the `domain:spec` seat as a follow-up card.** `IAutomationService.canonicalizeStoredFlow?(name, definition)` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts:853`) is unchanged; the protocol passes `options` structurally, and the one in-repo implementation honours it, but a second implementation that ignores a third argument would lift a retired spelling on a new flow silently — option A's behaviour behind a passing contract. The fix is a one-line optional `options?: { includeRetired?: boolean }` on the contract (the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` shape `todos?` took), spec-lane work outside ruling item 4's lane and outside this PR's claim; not blocking.
5. **Dev deviation 3 (the #4580 warning moved outside the claim's strict lines) — answered: right, see ① item 8.** Flow-only, inside protocol.ts, and required so a refused new flow never logs "was saved".
6. **Dev deviation 5 (`test:repo` not run locally) — answered by CI, partially at read time.** `Test Core (1/6)` and `(5/6)` concluded `success`; `Test Core (2/6)`, `(3/6)`, `(4/6)` and `(6/6)` were still `in_progress` at 2026-10-16T12:31Z (see the check-run paragraph below).
7. **Reviewer's own note — a publish-mode edge, consistent with the ruling's letter, no action.** A raw `PUT /api/v1/meta/flow/:name?mode=publish` of a legacy body over a name that holds ONLY a draft row (never published) reads the active address, finds none, and judges the save new — the same answer the OCC read gives at `:23517` ("the row the save overwrites"), and the ruling's "at the save's resolution scope". Studio never sends it (publish is a promotion, ① item 4), and `os migrate meta --stored` rewrites such a draft with `source` set. Named here so the maintainer sees the predicate's one asymmetric arm; a symmetric publish-reads-draft fallback is not asked for by any ruling item.
8. **Reviewer's own note — the two-round refusal for a bare loose wait key** (dev acceptance note 3) is the authoring funnel's own behaviour, pinned as equal; not a finding of this PR.
